newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher in selective trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher in selective trade.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher but well off their peaks in active trading on Thursday as the market contined to look for direction, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.78 percent, or 2.32 points, to 298.12 on all-share turnover of 181 million shekels against 130 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.46 percent higher at 304.72.
Traders said the session opened on strong demand with the Maof rising as much as 1.5 percent, but by midday prices started declining.
"During the last few days the market has been stuck and can't rise or fall. I think in the near term it will remain static," said Zvi Hoffman of Meitav Investments and Securities.

Yossi Weidelfeld of Eyal Securities said the volatile trading of the last several days showed that the market is looking for direction. "At the current level the market is very selective and trading is directionless," he said.

"This might be due to heavy trading by Maof speculators. Many investors prefer to sit on the fence until the expiry of the June contracts (on July 24), which is expected to be very stormy," Hoffman said, stressing that the market's trend is still positive.
"The market needs some rest before it starts rising again. It's only normal that after a sharp rise volume falls and the market stabilises," Weidelfeld added.

Delek the Israel Fuel Corp led the most actives, plunging 6.0 percent to 11,245 agorot on turnover of 19.1 million shekels. Delek fell on news that its Delek Automotive Systems subsidiary is being charged with tax evasion to the tune of 100 million shekels.
Delek Automotive fell 4.25 percent to 643 agorot.

Other active shares included Bezeq Israel Telecom, which fell 0.25 percent to 1,058 agorot on volume of 13.7 million shekels, and Koor Industries, which rose 3.5 percent to 35,857 agorot on volume of 6.7 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
